newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: New Dutch money market derivative launched.
newsitem.headline: New Dutch money market derivative launched.

text.p: Dutch dealers said on Thursday a new derivative had been introduced in the Dutch money market following the launch of an overnight Amsterdam Offered Rate (AIBOR) on Monday.
Dealers said the new product, the Amsterdam Interbank Overnight Average (AIONA) was derived from the existing Interest Rate Swap (IRS).

OHV (Oolders, Heijning and Voogelaar) moneybrokers confirmed they had acted as intermediary in the first overnight indexed swap between Rabobank Nederland and Bank Labouchere, but they declined to specify the amount of money involved in the deal.
AIONA compares the average overnight AIBOR rate for the contract period against a pre-determined rate of interest, with one of the two parties paying the difference at settlement.
"It is an exchange between a fixed and a variable rate," a dealer said.
"There seems to be quite a lot of interest in this new product, also from abroad," said a dealer at OHV, adding that deals could be done for amounts of 25 million guilders or more.
"Some 100 or 200 million guilders would be a normal size for a deal," he said.

On Monday the Dutch central bank began publishing an overnight AIBOR in response to demand from banks who had said they needed the new rate as a benchmark for business related to index-swaps and other derivatives.
Overnight AIBOR was fixed at 2.94 percent on Thursday.
Dealers said overall money market business was thin on Thursday with the decision by the German Bundesbank to leave rates unchanged having no impact on the market.
Market players expected the Dutch central bank to leave the Dutch special advances rate unchanged at 2.50 percent when it sets a new pact at 1500 GMT.
The guilder was virtually unchanged against the mark at 112.3175 per 100 marks from 112.315 on Wednesday.
